title: Gradient boosting predicts COVID-19 infection risk in nursing homes
summary: A gradient boosting model trained on 1,146 nursing homes in three states had cross-validation AUC 0.729. Risk indices generated on May 4 were prospectively validated against outcomes on May 11 for 1,021 California homes, with AUC 0.721, sensitivity 0.622 and specificity 0.713. County infection rate and number of separate units were the strongest predictors.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting algorithm on facility and community features
organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Out-of-sample prospective validation in a different state.
evidence.unknown: Discrimination is modest and predictions are facility-level. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient boosting model estimated each facility risk of having a confirmed COVID-19 resident.
